correctness.rationale: I independently enumerated the factors in order of their distinct partner of vertex 0, assigning a disjoint matching on the remaining six vertices at each step. This visits every unordered factorization exactly once. I generated neighbors by enumerating all three four-cycles on every four-element vertex subset, looking up the owners of opposite edge pairs, exchanging alternating edge ownership, and reanchoring; duplicate outcomes were collapsed. The resulting simple graph has 6240 vertices, 17640 edges and degree/count pairs (0,960), (3,1680), (7,2520), (9,420), (13,630), (21,30). Orbit traversal using adjacent transpositions reached the whole respective degree class from each of six representatives. The five positive-degree representative BFSs each reached 5280 states, with eccentricities 11,10,10,10,9 in that order. The affine representative was used for degree 21. Analytically, two factors have union 4+4 exactly when the matching involutions commute (their product has order 2 rather than 4); commuting factors generate a faithful transitive elementary abelian group and thus a regular group of order 8. The converse and normalizer count give the 30-state affine orbit. An isolated factorization has no 4+4 union and hence every pair is Hamiltonian. This verifies the original componentwise census, not a graph with persistent factor colors or longer switches.
residual_risks: The metric verification is exact finite computation, not proof-assistant formalization; no larger K_n is covered.

value.rationale: K8 is a natural finite case of the established intercalate switch problem. The fixed-label metric supplies a sharp move bound for any two mobile factorizations and identifies a canonical isomorphism orbit of best starting states. This answers a genuinely different reconfiguration question than orbit-quotient connectivity or a count of labelled designs.
residual_risks: No general growth claim about larger complete graphs or other moves.
